data_table.Clinical: Drowsy but rousable to voice, capillary refill 4 sec, cool peripheries, urine output 40 mL in last hour
data_table.Given so far (60 min): IV ceftriaxone and azithromycin, 30 mL/kg (2 L) Hartmann over 45 min
data_table.Bloods: Hb 128 g/L, WCC 22.4 x10^9/L, platelets 148 x10^9/L, urea 22 mmol/L, creatinine 240 micromol/L (baseline 148), lactate 4.8 mmol/L (from 3.2), bicarbonate 18 mmol/L
data_table.Bedside echo: Hyperdynamic LV, underfilled chambers, no valvular pathology, IVC 1.4 cm with >50% respiratory variation
data_table.Access: Femoral central venous catheter being placed

lead_in: What is the most appropriate next step in haemodynamic management?

options.text: Give 500 mL of 4 percent albumin bolus over 30 minutes and defer any vasopressor initiation until albumin has been given and haemodynamics reassessed at 30 minutes after infusion
options.rationale: Albumin can be considered when large volumes of crystalloid have been given but does not replace vasopressor for persistent hypotension after 30 mL/kg. (Source: Surviving Sepsis Campaign Guidelines 2021)

options.text: Continue further 30 mL per kilogram Hartmann bolus over 30 minutes and defer any vasopressor initiation until 60 mL per kilogram total crystalloid has been given as first line
options.rationale: Further large-volume fluid bolus in a patient already fluid-loaded risks pulmonary oedema; vasopressor is indicated after 30 mL/kg. (Source: Surviving Sepsis Campaign Guidelines 2021)

options.text: Commence intravenous dopamine 5 microgram per kilogram per minute via peripheral cannula targeting mean arterial pressure at least 65 mmHg and further 500 mL Hartmann bolus over 30 minutes
options.rationale: Dopamine is inferior to noradrenaline (increased arrhythmia, no mortality benefit) and is no longer first line in septic shock. (Source: Surviving Sepsis Campaign Guidelines 2021)

options.text: Commence intravenous vasopressin 0.03 unit per minute via the central venous catheter as first-line vasopressor targeting mean arterial pressure at least 65 mmHg and 500 mL Hartmann bolus
options.rationale: Vasopressin is a second agent added to noradrenaline (or noradrenaline-sparing) not a first-line vasopressor in septic shock. (Source: Surviving Sepsis Campaign Guidelines 2021)

options.text: Commence intravenous noradrenaline via the central venous catheter targeting mean arterial pressure at least 65 mmHg and give a further 500 mL Hartmann bolus with reassessment at 30 minutes
options.rationale: Septic shock with mean arterial pressure below 65 mmHg after 30 mL/kg crystalloid resuscitation warrants immediate noradrenaline initiation per Surviving Sepsis (do not wait for further fluid). (Source: Surviving Sepsis Campaign Guidelines 2021)

explanation.summary: Septic shock is a subset of sepsis with vasopressor requirement to maintain MAP at least 65 mmHg and lactate above 2 mmol/L despite adequate fluid resuscitation. Surviving Sepsis Campaign 2021 hour 1 bundle: measure lactate, obtain blood cultures, broad-spectrum antibiotics within 1 hour, crystalloid 30 mL/kg IV within first 3 hours for hypotension or lactate above 4 mmol/L, and vasopressor if hypotensive during or after fluid resuscitation to maintain MAP at least 65 mmHg. Noradrenaline is first-line vasopressor. Vasopressin 0.03 U/min is added when noradrenaline dose exceeds 0.25 to 0.5 microgram/kg/min. Adrenaline is third line. Dopamine is not preferred (increased arrhythmia, no mortality benefit versus noradrenaline). Peripheral noradrenaline is acceptable while central access is obtained, using a large-bore cannula in an antecubital or larger vein for a limited time to avoid extravasation. Hydrocortisone 200 mg IV daily is added for refractory shock requiring noradrenaline above 0.25 microgram/kg/min. Continue fluid resuscitation guided by dynamic markers of fluid responsiveness (passive leg raise, stroke volume variation, IVC ultrasound).
key_points: 30 mL/kg crystalloid within first 3 hours in sepsis-related hypotension or lactate above 4.
Start noradrenaline for MAP below 65 during or after initial 30 mL/kg fluid.
Vasopressin added when noradrenaline exceeds 0.25-0.5 microgram/kg/min.
explanation.pearls: Septic shock with MAP below 65 after 30 mL/kg crystalloid gets noradrenaline started immediately targeting MAP 65 mmHg, not more large-volume fluid or dopamine - noradrenaline is first-line vasopressor per Surviving Sepsis 2021.

subtopic_detail: Indication for urgent haemodialysis in acute kidney injury with hyperkalaemia refractory to medical therapy
stem:
You are the medical registrar reviewing a 68 year old man on the ward on day 4 of admission for community-acquired pneumonia. He has developed acute kidney injury on top of baseline chronic kidney disease stage 3 (baseline creatinine 148 micromol/L). He takes perindopril, hydrochlorothiazide and spironolactone for heart failure with reduced ejection fraction; the ACE inhibitor and spironolactone were stopped on day 2 of admission.

This morning he reports increasing shortness of breath and palpitations. On assessment he has pulse rate 58 per minute, blood pressure 152/92 mmHg, respiratory rate 26 per minute, oxygen saturation 92 percent on 4 L per minute nasal prongs, temperature 36.9 degC. Cardiovascular examination reveals no gallop, elevated jugular venous pressure at 6 cm and bilateral basal crackles. Investigations: potassium 6.8 mmol/L (yesterday 6.2), sodium 130 mmol/L, bicarbonate 12 mmol/L, urea 42 mmol/L, creatinine 480 micromol/L (baseline 148), venous pH 7.20, lactate 1.8 mmol/L. Electrocardiogram now shows sinus bradycardia with peaked T waves in V2 to V5, PR interval 240 milliseconds and a widened QRS at 130 milliseconds. In the past 30 minutes he has received intravenous calcium gluconate 10 mL of 10 percent, intravenous salbutamol nebulised 10 mg, insulin 10 units with dextrose 50 mL of 50 percent, and intravenous sodium bicarbonate 100 mmol. Urine output has been 20 mL in the last 4 hours.

data_table.Fluid status: Elevated JVP 6 cm, bilateral basal crackles, urine output 20 mL in 4 h
data_table.Bloods: K 6.8 mmol/L (yesterday 6.2), Na 130 mmol/L, bicarbonate 12 mmol/L, urea 42 mmol/L, creatinine 480 micromol/L (baseline 148), venous pH 7.20, lactate 1.8 mmol/L
data_table.ECG: Sinus bradycardia, peaked T waves V2-V5, PR 240 ms, QRS 130 ms
data_table.Given in last 30 min: Calcium gluconate 10 mL 10% IV, salbutamol 10 mg nebulised, insulin 10 units + dextrose 50 mL 50%, sodium bicarbonate 100 mmol IV
data_table.Medications: Perindopril and spironolactone stopped day 2, still on hydrochlorothiazide

lead_in: What is the most appropriate next step?

options.text: Urgent renal consult for haemodialysis access via femoral vascular catheter for immediate haemodialysis in the intensive care unit for hyperkalaemia refractory to medical therapy with pulmonary oedema
options.rationale: Refractory hyperkalaemia with widened QRS and ECG changes plus fluid overload plus severe uraemic acidosis meets multiple KDIGO indications for urgent renal replacement. (Source: KDIGO Clinical Practice Guideline for AKI (2012))
source_refs: KDIGO Clinical Practice Guideline for AKI (2012)

options.text: Give further intravenous calcium gluconate 10 mL of 10 percent bolus and repeat insulin 10 units with dextrose 50 mL of 50 percent bolus and reassess electrocardiogram at 30 minutes
options.rationale: Further temporising measures do not remove potassium and do not correct fluid overload or acidosis; definitive removal via haemodialysis is required. (Source: KDIGO Clinical Practice Guideline for AKI (2012))
source_refs: KDIGO Clinical Practice Guideline for AKI (2012)

options.text: Give oral sodium polystyrene sulfonate 30 g single dose and give intravenous frusemide 80 mg to promote diuresis and potassium excretion with reassessment of potassium at 60 minutes
options.rationale: Polystyrene sulfonate is slow (hours) and frusemide is ineffective in oligoanuric AKI; definitive removal via haemodialysis is required urgently. (Source: KDIGO Clinical Practice Guideline for AKI (2012))
source_refs: KDIGO Clinical Practice Guideline for AKI (2012)

options.text: Commence intravenous sodium zirconium cyclosilicate 10 g three times daily and repeat calcium gluconate 10 mL of 10 percent intravenous bolus and reassess the electrocardiogram at 30 minutes
options.rationale: Sodium zirconium is oral only, has onset over hours, and does not correct fluid overload or acidosis; not suitable for this life-threatening emergency. (Source: KDIGO Clinical Practice Guideline for AKI (2012))
source_refs: KDIGO Clinical Practice Guideline for AKI (2012)

options.text: Give continuous salbutamol nebulisation 10 mg per hour and repeat sodium bicarbonate 100 mmol intravenous with reassessment of potassium and arterial blood gas at 30 minutes after therapy
options.rationale: Repeat bicarbonate and beta-agonist temporise potassium shift but not fluid or uraemia; definitive removal via haemodialysis is required. (Source: KDIGO Clinical Practice Guideline for AKI (2012))
source_refs: KDIGO Clinical Practice Guideline for AKI (2012)

explanation.summary: Acute kidney injury requires urgent renal replacement therapy for AEIOU indications: Acidosis (severe metabolic, pH below 7.1 or bicarbonate below 10 mmol/L refractory to bicarbonate therapy), Electrolyte disturbance (hyperkalaemia above 6.5 mmol/L refractory to medical therapy or with ECG changes), Ingestion (dialysable toxin: methanol, ethylene glycol, lithium, salicylate, valproate), Overload (pulmonary oedema unresponsive to diuretics in oligoanuric patient), Uraemia (encephalopathy, pericarditis, bleeding). Medical management of severe hyperkalaemia: calcium gluconate 10 mL 10 percent IV (cardiac membrane stabilisation), insulin 10 units with 50 mL 50 percent dextrose IV (intracellular shift, effect at 15-30 min), salbutamol 10 to 20 mg nebulised (intracellular shift, additive), sodium bicarbonate 50 to 100 mmol IV (if severe acidosis), sodium polystyrene sulfonate 15-30 g PO or PR (gastrointestinal removal, slow onset). None of these definitively remove potassium in oligoanuric patients; dialysis is required. Frusemide is ineffective without residual urine output. Modality: intermittent haemodialysis is preferred if haemodynamically stable; continuous renal replacement therapy for haemodynamic instability.
key_points: AEIOU indications for urgent RRT: Acidosis, Electrolyte, Ingestion, Overload, Uraemia.
Refractory hyperkalaemia with ECG changes and oliguria requires urgent haemodialysis.
Frusemide is ineffective in oligoanuric AKI; medical measures only temporise potassium.
explanation.pearls: AKI with potassium 6.8 mmol/L, widened QRS, oligoanuria, pulmonary oedema and pH 7.20 refractory to full medical hyperkalaemia protocol has multiple KDIGO indications for urgent haemodialysis - further calcium and insulin only buy time.

sources.label: KDIGO Clinical Practice Guideline for AKI (2012)
